utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Today in the absence of Judge David, Judge Van Den Wyngaert and I sit pursuant to the provisions of Rule 15 bis. Did you have a matter, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Your Honours, I want to take a few minutes to address two issues with the Trial Chamber. First, last night just before midnight and just after midnight, the Defence disclosed two additional exhibits to the Prosecution. I'm not objecting to the introduction or disclosure of these exhibits, but do want to note for the record the lateness of them since it has been raised as an issue in the Prosecution case, and of course, we're not sure what appeals might be taken in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There are similar late disclosures by the Prosecution, if I remember. Probably not as late as midnight, but the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour. That's why I'm not objecting to them, but it seems that might important to note for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, the exhibits at issue are two maps of the area and a photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have yet to received the photograph. If that could be disclosed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The second matter, Your Honour, I'd like to raise with the Chamber is what I consider as some unfortunate advocacy by the Milan Lukic Defence team, and I want to request that the Chamber give some consideration to a suggestion that I wish to make. If the Chamber would be kind enough to give consideration to it over the recess. Judge Robinson, you were in New York last week at meetings in the United Nations headquarters, and I do not know if you have had time to review the transcript since your return. During a presentation on the 9th of December, Mr. Alarid spent over an hour asserting dozens of allegations not only addressed at the Prosecution but against others as well. I accepted Judge Van Den Wyngaert's suggestion to respond in writing, and I will not take any time today to do so orally. But in working on the written response, I have come to realize that an unfounded allegation cavalierly cast across the courtroom takes considerable time to respond to and is an unwelcome distraction from the important work of a trial. Some of the objections raised yesterday included gratuitous insults or accusations directed at me. I have reminded myself of what is contained in the Code of Professional Conduct for Counsel appearing before the International Tribunal, and I draw the attention of the Chamber to Article 27. Paragraph 27(A) states: "Counsel shall demonstrate respect, integrity and courtesy for officials and staff members of the Tribunal and for all persons who facilitate and participate in the proceedings." 27(C) states: "Counsel shall recognize the representatives of the parties as professional colleagues and shall act fairly, honestly, and courteously towards them." The unfounded attacks against my personal integrity last week, last week's correspondence from Mr. Alarid which characterized filings by the Prosecution with what seems to be an scatological reference as well as other intemperate language, and yesterday's inclusions of insults is a violation of the code of professional conduct, is unfair to me and members of my team, and I submit undermines the public perception of the dignity of these proceedings. I'm therefore requesting the Chamber to consider the following suggestions. First, each of you on this Bench, as individuals, is an experienced jurist. I believe when raising objections, a simple statement by any of the attorneys of the legal basis for the objection should be sufficient for you to recognize the issue to be decided. A simple statement such as relevance or leading question or lack of foundation, I would think, in most cases, be sufficient to inform the Chamber of the pertinent issue. I believe it should then be left to the Chamber to decide whether it wishes to hear additional information or argument on the matter. I believe this practice would go a long way to minimise statements that are unnecessary to the issue at hand and undermine the conduct of the trial. The second suggestion I ask the Chamber to consider over the recess is the following. The Chamber when called upon to make a decision must make it in an informed manner. It is entitled to rely on representations made by counsel appearing before it as officers of the court, trusting that those counsels will have checked their information and make whatever assertions they make in good faith. Yesterday, Mr. Ivetic made a statement that I had taken a particular position with respect to the Duga article's reliability. While I did not recall taking such a position, I was unable to immediately recall details of the prior discussions of the article. I asked a member of my staff to check the record yesterday evening, and she informed me yesterday evening that Mr. Ivetic has incorrectly characterized the prior discussions about the Duga article. I will not take any time with it here this morning, as I think the issue will arise again later in the trial. I do ask the Chamber to consider requiring the following, that advocates who are going to refer and characterize earlier discussions, particularly when such characterizations are going to be of a pejorative nature, that such only be done after checking the record and that a cite to the transcript be provided where possible so that attorneys and the Chamber can have the opportunity to review the transcript. I appreciate that objections must be raised quickly, but LiveNote has the capacity to navigate the trial record quickly. A simple search of the word "Duga" would have identified all discussions related to that evidence in a few seconds. I would greatly appreciate the Chamber giving due consideration to these requests over the holiday recess. Your Honours, the final point I wish to raise with you is my concern going into the holiday recess with no definitive witness list from the Milan Lukic Defence. I note that you yourself raised the issue yesterday, and I'm able to discuss it at any time you choose. I would simply ask that we do discuss it before concluding proceedings today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber has the submissions, the motion, filed by the Defence and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I believe we are still awaiting response from the Prosecution, and we'll give a decision and take into consideration all relevant factors, including those that you have raised. Please call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, our next witness will be MLD10, testifying subject to protective measures of pseudonym, voice distortion, and face distortion, and she will be presented viva voce, and I hope to cut her down to two hours. And perhaps I can inquire if Mr. Groome has confirmed that the translation offered yesterday for the exhibit was indeed with insertations from the Prosecution and when the proper translation will be available.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I haven't checked it yet, Your Honour. I'll ask Ms. Mazzocco here to see if she can get some additional information about the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit, and begin, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And if I could have the assistance of the usher, I have a pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, as you know, I'm Dan Ivetic, one of the attorneys for Milan Lukic, and for purposes of the record I'm going to have to address you today as MLD10, and in a moment you will be shown a pseudonym sheet. And now, madam, I'd ask you to take a look and review the sheet, and if you could confirm for us that the information as to yourself contained therein is correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you could please, then, also tell me if the -- if -- pardon me. If you have to refer to any of the other individuals listed on there - I believe there's one other individual listed on there - I would ask you to please use the pseudonym that is listed therein, if that's okay with you, and then I would ask you to sign this sheet or initial it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honours, I'd ask for this document to be introduced under seal as the next available 1D exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D 93 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, if you could tell me as we begin, what is your ethnicity or your religious national identity or affinity.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: By ethnicity, I'm Bosnian, Bosniak, and by religious affiliation, I'm Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. I'm just waiting for the translation and the transcript to catch up with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we can go briefly into private session, I'd like to address some matters that would perhaps identify the witness if handled in open court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Witness, we are now again in open session, so now from this point forward everything that we talk about will be transmitted publicly, so I again urge you to be careful not to reveal your identity and to use the information on the pseudonym sheet that has been left in front of you. With respect to the time period of the Bosnian civil war, did you have occasion to go to Bosnia-Herzegovina during that time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: You mean during the war? I did not go to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, given all the matters that we've discussed in closed session, would you consider yourself a person that knew Milan Lukic very well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In all the time that you've known Milan Lukic, has he ever had blond hair or blue eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How would you describe how Milan Lukic acted toward persons of different ethnic groups, that is to say, ethnic and religious groups different from his own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, I would say that Milan Lukic is very thoughtful and kind towards all people regardless of nationality, and he was on good terms with everyone in the broader region of Visegrad. I never heard about any excesses or any quarrels that he might have had with anyone. There was never any problem between him and our family, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can ask you, did you ever witness him to make any insults against persons that were of the Muslim religion or national identity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: No. I've never witnessed or heard about any such thing, and I maintain with full responsibility that he did not distinguish between people in terms of nationality or ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And again, I'm waiting just for the English translation and the transcript to catch up with us. If you could briefly give us your personal appraisal of the type of person Milan Lukic was based upon your -- based upon knowing him in your life. How is it that you would describe him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Milan Lukic was extremely handsome, a quiet, nice person, always forthcoming, helpful whenever he could be, an extremely humane and gracious person. Noble, even, I would say, a very positive character, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And MLD10, I would like to now draw your attention to the time period when the war broke out in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you recall when it was that the war broke out in your homeland of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: The war in my home country, Bosnia-Herzegovina, broke out in 1992, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now you've already told us that you were not present in Bosnia-Herzegovina during the duration of the war. Did you have family members who were caught up in the war and had to endure the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Only one of my brothers was not there. The rest of the family was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were any members of your family engaged as members of any of the armed forces participating in the war, and if so, which?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. The four of them were in the armed forces. One of them got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And which army did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: In the federal army, the Muslim army, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And ma'am, without revealing the exact location, when the war first broke out, where were your father and your siblings? What municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: In the municipality of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you lost contact with your father and your siblings or said contact was interrupted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I severed contacts with them from the time when the war broke out or, rather, all contacts were cut.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall a time period in 1992 when you sought out the assistance of Milan Lukic to ascertain the fate of your family members that were in Visegrad and to try and assist them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us some of the details about when it was precisely that you sought out Mr. Milan Lukic's assistance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, I called his sister in Belgrade. I wanted to talk to her. That was on the 8th, in the afternoon. I talked to her, and she told me that Milan was in Belgrade and that he wasn't there at the time, and I asked her to let him know that I wanted to meet him if possible because I wanted him to let me know what was happening with my family. And I told her that he should call me if possible, and she said that he would, and he indeed called me. That was on the 8th between 8 and 9 p.m. That was right after the evening news. So we talked. He asked me if I was married, how I lived. He inquired about my health, and I asked him if we could perhaps meet, and he said that we could and that the best thing to do would be to meet in Novi Pazar. I asked him why, whether any other place was an option, and he said that he had some things to do, that he was taking some Muslims from Visegrad to Novi Pazar, to get them away from the war zone. So we set up a meet in Novi Pazar, and I asked him if he could call me on the 10th to confirm the meeting in Novi Pazar, and then around 1.00 p.m. he called me, and we confirmed this meeting in Novi Pazar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can just back up a little bit. You indicated twice in your answer that events occurred on the 8th. Could you please clarify for us what month is in reference.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in your answer, you also mentioned the 10th for the meeting in Novi Pazar. Could you clarify for us and confirm for us the month and the year of that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: That was on the 10th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, being careful not to reveal any identities of yourself, can you tell us how you obtained the telephone number for Milan's sister in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, I had it written down somewhere, but I couldn't find the number, and then I called a neighbor of mine from Visegrad. She lived in Uzice, and she gave me her number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the meeting in Novi Pazar, could you explain for us exactly what did you agree with Milan Lukic for the 10th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: On the 10th of June, 1992, Milan and I arranged that he should try to find my family, to see whether they were okay, whether they needed anything, where they were, and I sent some stuff with him. I think it was a pack of cigarettes and maybe a kilo of coffee and 100 Deutschemarks. I gave it to him so that he could give it to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we've been talking about these two dates, the 8th and the 10th of June, 1992. How is it that those particular dates stand out in your mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, it stuck in my mind because my husband had come back from Germany some seven days before that. It's my birthday on the 13th of June, and we always have a celebration as much as we could. My husband came -- well, it's a well known date throughout the world. It's the Feast of St. Anthony of Padua, and that's my birthday, and he used to joke and call me Antonia for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I can ask you, did Milan Lukic at that time tell you why he had been in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: He told me that his mother was supposed to undergo some check-ups or some examinations on the 7th, and that's why he came to Belgrade. She had to do some ultrasound check-ups. That's why he had come to Belgrade with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can help out with -- for those who are not familiar with the geography of the region, where is Novi Pazar located in relation to, let's say, Belgrade and Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, it's about halfway between Belgrade and Montenegro, the place where I had set off from. It's close to the border of Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was there a specific location or landmark in Novi Pazar that was the site of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: We arranged that we would meet next to the fortress, because that was the easiest thing to do, because you could ask anyone anywhere where the fortress was, and that's how we met.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you indicated that was so it'd be easier for you to meet. Could you tell us how it was that you traveled there. By what means did you travel there, and with whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I traveled there in our car with my husband. We had a Mercedes. It was a diesel engine, 2.5 litre. The model was 190.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you detail for us the route that you took to travel from your place of residence and the fortress -- or Novi Pazar, I should say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, it was Bar, Podgorica; Podgorica, Ivangrad; and then from Ivangrad, Rozaje, Novi Pazar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall the approximate time that you spent traveling to Novi Pazar from your home and/or the time -- the approximate time that you arrived at the fortress that was to be the meeting point for your encounter with Mr. Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I think it took us about four hours. We took breaks en route. We were not in a hurry. We had enough time to get there on time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall the approximate time when you arrived at the fortress?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, we arrived there about one -- half an hour earlier. We didn't want to get there too early. That's why we stopped on our route there, to avoid that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In terms of the time of day, what time of day was it in reference to either the morning, afternoon, evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: It was in the evening, between 5 -- or, rather, I'm sorry, between 7 and 8 p.m. That's when we arranged to meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you have any difficulty find the fortress? How did you find the fortress for the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, I asked the police in town where the fortress was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did in fact Milan Lukic arrive for the encounter or meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us, do you have an estimation as to the duration of that meeting with Milan Lukic at the Novi Pazar fortress?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, 15 minutes to half an hour, not more than that, 15 minutes to half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us -- could you tell us what transpired during that meeting? What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, we said hello. I asked him whether he saw my family, whether he had heard from anyone where they were, and he explained to me that he would do his best to locate them and that he had some knowledge as to the fact that my father had to report to the police station in Visegrad and that he would do his best to find them as soon as he got back from Novi Pazar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned earlier a package or gift package that you'd prepared for your relatives. Did you have occasion to give that to Milan Lukic, and what was his response to your request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, I handed it over to Milan, and he promised that he would in turn hand it over to them and that he would make a 100-per cent effort to find them, that he would do all he could do to help them, morally and financially and in any other way. And that allayed my fears because I didn't know my mother at all, so my father was everything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you indicated you traveled there with your husband. Did your husband participate in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. My husband just said hello and he stood there. He didn't make any comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Lukic arrive alone, or were there other people in the vehicle with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Lukic told me that his mother was with him, and then I asked to see her if possible because I wanted to say hello to her. He told me that I could but that he was in a hurry, that I could just say hello to her briefly. So we went to the car that Milan had driven there. It was a blue car. His mother was inside, and he opened the passenger-side door. His mother got out. We said hello. We talked for five minutes, and I told her I wished her a safe trip, and then they went off.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You indicated that Milan had promised to do everything in his power to find your relatives and to pass along the gift packet that you had prepared for them. Did you ever have an opportunity to confirm with your family members whether Milan gave this gift packet to them as you had requested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I did not have an opportunity during the war to talk to anyone. After the war, I managed to find my people in Zenica. They had moved to Zenica, and they told me everything. My father was still alive at the time, and he told me how Milan was helping them, how he invited them over to their place, how he hid them, how they slept in their place, how he gave them food, how he managed to make it possible for them to move to a safe place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. I believe we're going into an area that's outside the Rule 67 alibi notice and beginning to speak about events on the 26th and 27th of June, which was not -- we were not given notice that this witness would be testifying as to these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I direct Mr. Groome to Rule 65 ter, which is the instructive rule as to testimony of witnesses. This witness was properly disclosed under Rule 65 ter within the time periods that the Court set for 65 ter notification by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: His point, Mr. Ivetic, as I understand it, is that the area that is now being discussed doesn't relate to the alibi. I'm not sure that I agree with Mr. Groome, but it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I'm wrong, but maybe Mr. Ivetic would be able to clarify for the Chamber. The event that she's now referring to, what is the date of that event. If we could have clarification, then perhaps I'll withdraw my objection if it's a different day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, she's talking about multiple events. I mean, if you want to go through the whole litany, I don't know. But we're not presenting her as an alibi that she was with Milan Lukic on any other date apart from the date that we have disclosed her as for and that she has just completed testifying about, and I leave it to Your Honours' instruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The way that I see it, Mr. Groome, she testified that she gave Milan Lukic a package for her family, and I think it is entirely reasonable to inquire whether that package had been delivered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just be heard briefly on this. There's another witness on the Defence witness list --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Should we be speaking in front of the witness with this? I don't know what Mr. Groome is bringing up now, but it sounds like he's bringing up discussions, so I don't know if the witness ought be excused or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no, we -- go along.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The relative of this witness is also scheduled to testify who testifies that -- what I believe she's about to testify to, that this event of saving her father and brother occurred on the 26th to the 27th of June. The alibi notice for this witness says nothing about that, and although there is a reference in the 65 ter about a good conduct of Milan Lukic with respect to treatment of her family, the 65 ter doesn't even say that date. So if this woman is now going to testify that on the 26th and 27th of June that Milan Lukic was present at the family home and did something with respect to her family, that clearly is something that we have not been given notice about with respect to Rule 67. I have no objection to her testimony about the 10th of June. That was properly noticed, and I'm not objecting to that. It's simply I believe we're going into an area now that we're talking about the 26th and 27th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you understand the objection now, Mr. Ivetic, that you have brought her to testify about the 10th, to provide an alibi for the 10th, but what --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that -- that -- I apologize.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But you appear to be now going beyond that to the 26th and 27th, different -- are you going in that direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can read for the record what the 65 ter description for this witness was. It says: "This witness is a character and alibi witness. MLD10 will testify as to the good acts and deeds of Milan Lukic, including how he saved members of her own family and brought Bosnian Muslims to Novi Pazar to escape the war zone. MLD10 will testify that Milan Lukic was in Serbia on 10 June, 1992, what he met with this witness. MLD10 will further address, rebut the testimony of VG-138." This is not merely an alibi witness, Your Honour. She is a mixed witness of alibi, fact, and character. She is properly disclosed for multiple areas. The only alibi that we are presenting her for is 10 June 1992. That is the only alibi testimony that she was disclosed for. We are seeking to and have disclosed her as a witness to testify as to her knowledge of the good deeds and acts of Milan Lukic towards her family and towards others. We do not -- she obviously cannot be an alibi witness for any of those as to specific dates because she was not present with him when he was saving or helping members of her family. So to the extent that she can recall the time periods when this was involved, she -- we're calling her to address her knowledge from her family of the good deeds and acts of Milan Lukic that I think go towards establishing the type of person he was, go toward mitigation and other factors that are relevant to these proceedings. So I would defer to Your Honours' instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So if I understand you, you're saying that in respect of the 26 and 27th, she will not be giving alibi evidence? She will be testifying to the good deeds, the character of the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We can ask her if she can pin it down to a time period, but, I mean, she's not an -- an alibi is someone who's with them or saw them. Obviously, she was nowhere -- she testified that she saw him on the 10th of June. She's not going to testify that she saw him on the 27th or the 26th of June or any other date unless -- unless we -- any other date related to the indictment. That's the crux of our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean, clearly if she says that, My father told me that he was with Milan Lukic on the 26th or 27th, the fact that she wasn't physically present with him doesn't mean that that evidence isn't relevant to alibi, and I think it's important to point out that I bear the burden on alibi. They just have to raise the reasonable possibility that Milan Lukic was not in Visegrad, but I must prove beyond reasonable doubt, and that's why Rule 67 gives me certain procedural rights and certain notice. I think the key documents to look at are the alibi notice that was served with respect to this witness. I read from it, and this is the notice of the 18th of July:

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we have a redaction of her relative's place of birth since this is a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: "... was burned down because they were Muslims, the Lukic family invited them to sleep at their place for the next few days. MLD2 will state in his testimony that between the period of 26 June 1992 until 29th June 1992, that he was at the house of Mile and Milan Lukic, and Milan -- that Milan Lukic did not leave the property at all during that time period." That's the notice that we've been given with respect to MLD 2. I believe what's appropriate here is we've not been given any notice that this witness is going to talk about that event, that this witness be not permitted -- if MLD 2 is going to come here and testify to that event, that has been properly noticed and he can properly testify about it. Otherwise, what's happened here, Your Honour, is that a new alibi witness has been raised for the first time in the middle of the testimony of the witness, and we've been given no notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I must correct a misstatement on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. I'm going to consult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, if indeed you were not notified of this matter, so that are you not in a position to rebut it, what would be the prejudice if we were to give you permission to rebut it at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may interject, Mr. Groome is incorrect that he was not put on notice. The statement of this witness that was disclosed in the alibi filings, and we could pull it up on the screen if need be. The last paragraph of that statement states: "Later, after the war, my father told me that Milan Lukic saved the family, and that my father and my brother slept and ate in Milan Lukic's house and that it was thanks to this that they survived." So this area that I'm going into has been disclosed as of July 8th of this year --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now does it relate --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- to Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- does it relate to the 26th and 27th, which is his point?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I haven't asked her about the 26th or the 27th. I've asked her about whether she heard from her family that Milan Lukic helped them and assisted them, and that's exactly what's been disclosed. And therefore, I take great issue with Mr. Groome for how he claims that everyone else is misrepresenting things here, but time and time again, the documentation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel is kindly asked to slow down for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... -- I really don't know what to do about this, and I apologize for [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, he's saying that you're premature. We don't know yet whether he's going to lead evidence about the 26th and 27th, so let us see how it develops and maybe you can take your point then if it is necessary. Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I will have to try and go back to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, madam -- madam, you had started testifying about when you had moved to Zenica and had met up with your family, that is to say your brother -- pardon me, your father, and they told you everything -- could you please try to complete your answer to my question, which originally was that: Did you ever have an opportunity to confirm with your family members whether Milan gave this gift packet to them as you had requested him to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. My father confirmed that, and so did my brother. They said that they had received the package, and they spent a couple of days in his house, that he helped them as much as he could, and that he even roasted some lamb for them. It was St. Vitus Day, and he said, Well, we'll roast a lamb to celebrate, and they spent some three or four days at his place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I don't think the point is premature, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It was St. Vitus Day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's the relevant day in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, as I was saying earlier, my interest really is getting in all the evidence. The rules do require that you be notified, and you have not been notified in relation to this particular aspect of this witness's evidence. Fairness, therefore, requires that you be given an opportunity to rebut it, and the Chamber will provide you with that opportunity at a later stage in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I guess, Your Honours, it's part of a greater concern that I have that hopefully we'll discuss later on, but there's another witness, MLD13, who has been noticed to us -- originally was an alibi for Pionirska but now is Bikavac. It's very hard to conduct a trial from a Prosecution point of view, particularly in an alibi case where the alibi is evolving or is changing. Clearly this witness, we were never given notice she was going to provide an alibi for Bikavac in the alibi notice that was filed, and I must note, late, but it was only under the order of the Court that it was eventually filed after the commencement of trial on the 18th of July. I take the Chamber at its word that will give me a fair opportunity to rebut this, but aside from that, Your Honour, just in terms of procedural fairness, again, it is me that has a very heavy burden to disprove this alibi. It is really very difficult for me to do it if the Defence is going to be permitted to change the alibi as we move through the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the alibi is not changing. The alibis that were presented, we're not adding any new people that were present with Milan Lukic. We're not adding any new dates or instances. The alibi, the factual basis for the alibis, which is what we were required to disclose, we disclosed. It hasn't changed, unlike what Mr. Groome has said. The alibis are what they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the way that I have practiced law all my life is that I am more concerned with substance --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- and with form and with procedure. So when you look at the rule on alibi, the purpose of that Rule which requires notice is to enable the Prosecution to have time to rebut it, and I have said I'm going to give Mr. Groome that time so that he can rebut it if he can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I have no problem with that. They have an absolute right to rebut any evidence I bring. The point is, I take umbrage with the statement that the alibi is changing when it's the same factual circumstance. If they rebutted as to the alibi witness, they can rebut any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is a matter for the Chamber to determine. We'll look at all the evidence and make up our mind about that. So proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam Witness, if we could return back in time to the conclusion of your meeting on the 10th of June, 1992, at Novi Pazar with Milan Lukic. You'd indicated earlier, I believe, that Milan Lukic had left after some time. Following your meeting with Milan Lukic, did you and your husband have occasion to go straight home, or did you go elsewhere, but for purposes of your safety, don't say in open court the -- don't say in open court either location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: My husband and I went to see a friend in Novi Pazar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honours, if we could briefly go into private session, I can deal with the identity of this friend and several other matters into the next area of my question that also ought to be in private session, so that we can effectively use the court time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We still have time, don't we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic. Let's leave it at yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just continuing my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now we're in open session, ma'am, so again, I caution you as to providing any details that might identify yourself. With respect to OTP witness Hamdija Vilic, in a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, specifically I believe it's paragraph 5 of the same, he says that during the war he lived in Zlijeb, Visegrad, together with his family. Can you, based upon your knowledge, tell us what you can about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Hamdija Vilic did not live in Zlijeb. He had a house in Prelovo. That's where he lived with his family. His house was allegedly burned down, and in fact it was burned down, but what I know is that his family was burnt in that house in Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, I'm waiting for the transcript and translations to catch up with you. What about -- again, without giving more than the -- more than what is at minimum necessary, what about Mr. Vilic's claim that you yourself are from Zavidovici?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We may need a redaction. I don't know how large the municipality she mentioned at line 20 is, but we may need to have that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- we can have that redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, madam, with respect to Mr. Hamdija Vilic, in the time that you've known him, has he gone by any nicknames, and if so what nicknames has he gone by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: His nickname is Zuti, meaning yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just so we can be sure that we're talking about the same person, Mr. Hamdija Vilic, how would you describe him? Is there any physical attribute that can differentiate him from any of his other brothers or anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, he's different because he has yellow hair, sun spots on his face. He does not have the lower arm.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure that the witness said this, but apparently she did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you say he does not have the lower arm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He does not have one part of his arm. The lower arm is missing on one side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge of whether Mr. Hamdija Vilic, nicknamed Zuti, was in fact a combatant of the Bosnian Muslim army and/or a commander of any unit in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes, he was, from what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to also ask you a bit more about him. Do you have knowledge or information about the incident that was raised during Mr. Vilic's testimony, his conviction and his gaol sentence after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I do know he was convicted after the war for two murders and for wounding I believe three persons with a hand grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And these persons that were either murdered or wounded, what ethnic or national identity were the victims of Hamdija Vilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to Mr. Hamdija Vilic, did you at any time tell Mr. Vilic that you were to be a witness for the Defence of Mr. Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were you afraid of Mr. Vilic, and if so, why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, I was afraid and I am still afraid of him because he's the kind of person that he is, if he killed some of his fellow combatants, former fellow combatants, with a hand grenade in a bar and he's never sober. He's constantly hanging around bars and drinking. And during the war, his brothers and he were notorious were brawls and excesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned his brothers. Could you give us a little more detail about your familiarity of his siblings, names and what you know about them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: The eldest brother is called Adem. He lives in Sarajevo. He, too, lost a leg in the war. Another brother, Hasan, lives in Austria. And there is also Hussein, who allegedly got killed. And another one died before the war while serving in the army. His name was Ramzija [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did there come a time when Mr. Hamdija Vilic requested to meet at your home with members of the Defence team of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. He asked to meet with the Defence counsel of Milan Lukic, and he said in those words, I can't meet with them in Sarajevo because the balijas - using that term - are following me everywhere in Sarajevo; I would be in danger; I want to be a protected witness; and if I can come, I can only accept to meet them at your place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the time frame or the day or the month when this meeting in question took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly the date. That was the same date when I gave a statement. My statement was given on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was Mr. Hamdija Vilic present in the room when you were meeting with the members of the Defence team and they were taking your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: No. Hamdija Vilic was in a different room with my husband, and I was in a different room. Also, music was playing, and he was not able to hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vilic -- Mr. Hamdija Vilic claimed here under oath and under penalty of perjury that there was an American attorney and a Serbian attorney present from the Milan Lukic Defence team that day at your home and that the American spoke Serbian badly. I ask you, madam, were there any American attorneys in your house that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: There were no American lawyers in my home. Both counsel spoke Serbian. I doubt that either of them spoke English at all, and these two were of Serbian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did these members of the Defence team of Milan Lukic introduce themselves to both yourself and to Mr. Hamdija Vilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how did they introduce themselves to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: They introduced themselves as a team of investigators and counsel. One was Vlado or Vladimir or something like that, and the other one was Mihailo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did in fact Mr. Hamdija Vilic on that occasion volunteer to be a witness for the defence of Milan Lukic and meet with these members of the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. He asked to appear as a witness, but he didn't want to meet with them in Sarajevo but to meet with them at my place, and I accepted, although he was not a very close relative and I didn't really feel like receiving anyone at my house. I expressed my wish to go to Sarajevo, but when he said he wasn't willing to meet with Sarajevo [as interpreted], I told the lawyers that they should come to my house instead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hamdija Vilic has made an allegation that he was offered 100.000 Euros for him to testify. What can you tell us about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Nobody offered him a single dinar, let alone 100.000. But before the lawyers came, he was saying he was willing to come here and give evidence and everything, but he says then, Five heads in my family are missing, each one of them is worth 20.000, so if they are willing to pay 100.000, then I'll come and testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we can perhaps have the tape checked later. I believe she said [B/C/S spoken], testify as to the truth, at the end of that, but that -- I don't want to take up time doing that now with asking her to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How did the persons present in your house react to Mr. Hamdija Vilic's demand to be paid 100.000 Euros to come and testify at the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: They were flabbergasted. They said, We have nothing more to talk about with you. If that's the way it is, there's nothing to talk about. We don't pay witnesses, and we can't give you any money.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Vilic at that -- at some point in time leave your home, and when I say Mr. Vilic, I mean Mr. Hamdija Vilic. Did he leave your home, and what can you tell us about the taxi ride that he, at least in his statement, talked about, which I guess he's testified that it really was his vehicle and no taxi.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes, he came in his own car, a ramshackle Volkswagen Golf. He parked his car there, and when I had to go and have my statement notarized in court, I asked him to wait a little. I told him, Wait a while while I get some food. Don't go. And then my husband later told me that as soon as I had left, he said, I want to leave now, immediately, will you please move your car. I want to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you tell Mr. Hamdija Vilic that you were going to have your statement notarized?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: No. I told him I was going to town. Since they were going back, I'll use that to get a ride to get some food because all I had was some frozen meat and I couldn't wait for it to defrost. I wanted to do some shopping and get something to eat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You said "since they were going back." Who is the "they" that you reference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: The lawyers, the Defence counsel. Since they were going back, I meant to go to town with them. I didn't tell him why I was going to town. Instead, I told him I was going to buy some food.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And madam, after this incident in your home, did Mr. Hamdija Vilic have occasion to contact you subsequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: He called me only once on the telephone. I answered, and he asked me, Are the lawyers calling you? I said, No, why would they? And I said nothing more. I just hung up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How did you interpret and regard this telephone call from Mr. Hamdija Vilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, my thinking was, as soon as he called me, that he had been to the Office of the Prosecutor or perhaps some other organizations down there to make that telephone call, that he was not calling from home, because otherwise he never called me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was that before or after he testified here at the Tribunal, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Hamdija Vilic ever tell you anything that would lead you to believe that he was involved with either the Bosnian or the Tribunal Prosecutor's Office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely when I talked to him before he came to my house, he told me that Bakira and I don't know who else were taking him to Visegrad every day practically for tours and I don't know what, and he said, They are harassing me, I have to go there every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you please enlighten --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We're going into an entire area here that I -- this is -- I mean, I'm aghast. I just have absolutely no notice of it. The only reference that we have in the 65 ter summary is MLD10 will further address the testimony of VG-138. That's hardly a summary of -- or an adequate summary of what we're hearing now. I mean, we should certainly have been given notice that she's -- about the kind of evidence that she's giving here now. I mean, how am to be I able to prepare for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, Hamdija Vilic was previously identified to us as VG-138. However, no protective measures were sought for him, and he testified under his formal name here in court. The 65 ter notice that we provided for this witness, that we had indicated would be a live witness, was that she would address and rebut the testimony of Hamdija Vilic. They have opened the door by bringing in Mr. Vilic to make -- for that wide series of very serious allegations against the members of the team, the members -- witnesses, and they full well knew considering Mr. Vilic in his testimony mentioned this witness multiple times, in his statement mentioned this witness multiple times. To say that they were not put on notice, that this witness when she was brought here to testify would testify as to Mr. Vilic, attack those spurilous allegations of Mr. Vilic, address the character of Mr. Vilic, and address reasons why he might be lying or testifying untruthfully when he was here is simply baffling. He knew full well that we were attacking Mr. Vilic's representations and his testimony, and they knew that this witness was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Groome, in our view, you have had enough notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, madam, I'd like to back up, and I have to -- I apologize, I have to scroll up to see where we left off before the objection. Let me see if you had finished. Yes. You mentioned in your response at page 39, lines 19 through 22, that Bakira and others were taking him to Visegrad every day. Do you have knowledge of this individual that he identified as Bakira? Can you give us any further information as to the identity of this Bakira?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Bakira is a woman from Visegrad who is involved with Muslims, the victims. That's what I know, that she's discharging those duties. I don't know any details about her. I know that she's doing that because when my brother's funeral was, she attended it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, is she part of any group or organization?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. She is in this group for the exhumation of the dead, dealing with those issues in general, for the Muslims, the missing Muslims, something like that. I don't know what it's called, but I know that that's what she does because she was in this organization when my brother was buried in Sarajevo, when we moved him from the Zepa area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And ma'am, now, what about the allegations and testimony of Mr. Vilic. I believe in open court but also in his statement, specifically, paragraph 18 of his statement, where he claimed that in your house the members of the Milan Lukic Defence team had a bag of money the size of a laptop computer. Did you see anything of that sort in your house the day when Hamdija Vilic met with members of the Defence team of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: They didn't have anything else in their trunk. Vladimir had a backpack with a laptop and nothing else. Mihailo didn't have anything. He didn't carry anything. Vlado was in a pair of shorts. Vlado [as interpreted] was wearing jeans, so I didn't see them bring in anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did they in fact use the laptop computer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. They used it to take my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness MLD10, have you ever been offered money by any member of the Defence team of Milan Lukic to testify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: No, never. No one. And no one ever does that, and there wouldn't have been any need because I wouldn't have come here had anyone offered me any money. Even if I had more money, I would have offered some for Milan Lukic's Defence, to assist with his defence. I would go that far. I would never, ever accept any money. I don't need any money. I have a regular income. I have enough money.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to move to a different area. Apart from the fears that you have expressed as to Hamdija Vilic, have you had occasion to experience any threat, intimidation, or pressure from third or unknown persons; and if so, what form did that activity take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. At one point in time, my home phone kept ringing all the time, and then I would hear this sound in the phone, and then they would say, You will see where you will go back to. I didn't know at that time -- well, I didn't know who that was because they didn't say their name. It lasted for about 15 days. I had to go and get the cordless phone to be able to get caller ID. But ever since I have been using the cordless phone, I have not received any calls of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And have you had anything else of this nature occur apart from the telephone -- the unknown telephone calls?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, I was in a situation to notice unknown vehicles pass by my house because I knew all the people from the neighbourhood passing by. I know their vehicles, and I know those persons. But recently, I have been seeing cars that I have not seen before, cars that pass by.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, madam, without mentioning that person's name in open session, could you tell us, what happened with the support person that was supposed to travel and accompany you -- travel with and accompany you here to The Hague? Did she in fact make the trip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: She was supposed to travel with me and be my escort, but when I was supposed to get a copy of her passport to send it in for a visa application, she simply gave up, and she said, Well, I don't want to, I don't dare, I can't. She didn't want to give me the reason why, and throughout the time she -- previous time, she kept saying that she would accompany me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to go into private session to go into more details as to this with respect -- with the aim of protecting the identity of this witness and also the third party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Madam, my name is Dermot Groome, and I'll be asking you some questions, and I, too, will refer to you as MLD10 to protect your identity. The first question I'd like to ask you is: How old were you when you left Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, I was probably 34, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The area that you've described as the area that you came from, are you also familiar with the area that's referred to as Zupa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that witness -- that Defence Exhibit 1D 94 be placed on the ELMO beside the witness, and I ask that she be given a blue pen. I see that you've used a red pen for the markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'm going to ask that you be shown one of the maps that you made markings on earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Madam, I'm advised it would be difficult to do that now, so I'm going to go to another area of inquiry, and they're going to try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: To assist the Prosecutor, the two maps were finally up loaded into e-court and we could probably give them the numbers and work with the digital copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I might just inquire, I only want to work with the one that has the broader area. Which one is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So I'd ask that 1D 22-5303 be called up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, you should see that in the screen in front of you. I believe it'll be to your right, and if I could ask, with the assistance of the usher, that the pen be made in blue so, again, we know that it's your markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The court deputy has an announcement to make about the map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are unable to locate the maps in e-court yet. I would suggest that the Prosecution would make the markings in blue on the same Defence exhibit, and I will cross-reference this for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. Sensible solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If that could be placed, it will be placed in hard copy, like you saw it before. You'll be given a blue pen, and as that's being prepared for you, what I would ask you to precisely as you're able if the area known as Zupa is on that map, would you please draw the boundary of it or the approximate boundary of it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: All this area from Zupa [as interpreted] up to the last stop, Kamenica, further up from Rujiste, is called Zupa. I don't know how to mark it. It's a whole area from Visegrad to the last bus stop at Kamenica. This whole area is called Zupa.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: At page 53, line 2, it should read, "All this area from Visegrad up to the last stop."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, before you make any mark, is it your testimony that everything depicted on the map is Zupa, or is it on one side of the Drina or the other? Let me just understand how you define Zupa before I ask you to make any marks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: To the right of the Drina River, all the villages from Visegrad to Rujiste. All the areas -- all the villages around this area are called Zupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So I would then ask you with the blue pen to please draw a line around the approximate boundaries of Zupa and just write "Zupa" inside it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, this whole area here. The only thing I can do is just extend this line here, to circle this area down to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If you would do that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: This whole area to the right, from Rujiste to Visegrad. You have the mountains here, the hills, and all those villages are part of Zupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. Please circle all the villages that are part of Zupa, please. They don't have be individual circles. Just one large circle to encompass all of Zupa.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, that's what I said. It's all the way up, but in fact, the problem is that this pen is not working. This whole region to the right of the Drina River all the way up to Rujiste and Kamenica. It's called Zupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We're getting you a working pen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, just -- in dyslexia I misspoke. It's 1D 220503 is electronic and 0503, not 5303.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Maybe we'll find it now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of this down to Visegrad. Yes, well, like this. To Visegrad, our people call all this area Zupa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you asked her to use a blue pen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I wasn't really all that precise, but this whole area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The blue pen is so close to the colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I thought a red pen was used before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I know, but I'm just saying it's not very easy to distinguish it from the colour of the rest of the map. Anyway, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you simply to write now "Zupa" inside the circle that you've drawn.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, Zupa is the area from Visegrad town going northward to Rujiste on the right bank of the Drina River; is that correct? Or the eastern bank of the Drina River; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'm finished with that exhibit. Now, how long has your family --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Actually, can we go into private session for this. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Madam, we're in public session. If I ask you any question that you think you would need to give information that would reveal your identity, please let me know before you answer. When did Milan Lukic leave the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, Milan Lukic left even before the 1990s. I know he went to Switzerland. He lived there for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to approximate the year that he left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I can't, because I didn't meet with him, so I couldn't tell you which year. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: From the time that he left Rujiste or Visegrad until the time you say you saw him on June of 1992, had you seen him during that time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I saw him once again in 1990, and I didn't even recognize him on that occasion. I asked the brother who was with me, Who is this boy, because he had grown up so fast, and my brother said, It's Milan Lukic. I'm sorry. What caught my eye was that he was so nicely dressed, so handsome, tall. I hadn't seen him for a long time before that, and I didn't recognize him immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After this time that you saw him in the company of your brother in 1990, did you see him again before you saw him in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Since you saw him in June of 1992, have you seen him again, have you been in his presence again until today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: No. I saw him on television once.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have any difficulty in recognizing him here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I did not have any difficulty. He's just older and heavier, stouter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When was the last time you had contact with any member of his family in Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: That was before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And have you had any contact after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: That's before I left. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So even on those occasions when you say you'd like to return to the family property once a year, you don't call in on the Lukic family and see how they're doing and have a cup of coffee or something to that order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether they're there still at all. I don't know whether they're still in Rujiste or not. I know nothing about that because I never went back, not even after the war to Rujiste. I once went to Prelovo to get my birth certificate and the certificate of citizenship, and I never went any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So ma'am, is it your evidence that you've never returned to see your property in Rujiste. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Not since the war ended, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who has told you that the house was overgrown and the condition that you described? Who gave you that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: My stepmother went there and my brother and my father while he was still alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about your statement. In paragraph 4 of your statement, you say the following: "I met with Milan at the agreed time and place," and this is in reference to your meeting on the 10th of June. "I met with Milan at the agreed time and place. He told me he had driven over some Muslim friends of him who were from the area of Visegrad and that he did not have much time, that his mother was in the car waiting for him to go back to Bosnia." My question to you is, is it your testimony that Milan Lukic told you that the people that he had driven from Visegrad were friends of his?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. He said he had brought with him some people - Muslims, that's how he explained it - from the area Visegrad. As to whether they were his friends or not, that he didn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So in your statement taken earlier this year where you say: "He told me that he had driven over some Muslim friends of his ...", that is something that you're no longer sure he said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I know he said Muslims, and I don't remember about friends. It's possible that he said Muslim friends, but I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'm going to ask that the statement be put up before you so you can take a look at it. It is 1D 22-0090, and again, it should appear on the screen to your right. And when it does appear, it's the last sentence of the paragraph. Have you been able to read the passage I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that in the statement that you gave a few months ago that you did say that Milan Lukic told you that they were his friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that I stated that. I did say Muslim friends, but maybe I added that. He didn't say whether he -- whether they were his friends or not. He said Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you have a specific recollection today as you sit here that he did not use the word "friends." Is that what you're saying now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In paragraph 5 of your statement, and I believe it'll be left up on the screen, so feel free to refer to it, you say that after you asked Milan Lukic to say hello to his mother, that he took you over to a car, and I quote: "Milan took me to a blue car, opened the co-driver's door, helped his mother out to say hello to me." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Had you ever seen that car before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: You mean his car, that particular car, or a car like that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That particular car.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: No, I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you have a clear recollection that it was blue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes, that much I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to describe anything else about the car, the make, the model, anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know because I didn't pay attention. It wasn't important to me. I don't normally look at makes of cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, let me read another portion of your statement from paragraph 5, in which you describe a conversation with Milan Lukic's mother: "She said Milan had driven her to Belgrade for some medical check-ups." Do you remember saying that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, in your testimony here today at page 19, line 4, you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I just realized that the statement that's up on the screen I hope is not being published. It's got the unredacted name of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The statement will not be broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'd like to ask you about something you said earlier today at transcript page 19, line 4, records you as saying: "He" -- referring to Milan Lukic, "he told me that his mother was supposed to undergo some check-ups or some examinations on the 7th and that is why he had come to Belgrade with her." Is it your evidence that he told you that that -- those appointments were for the 7th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you quite sure about that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. I am sure about that date because when I called Draginja, his sister, she said Milan was there, that she had ultrasound exam appointment for the 7th, that he was out, but as soon as he comes back she'll tell him to call me back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there any conversation about what ailment Mrs. Lukic was suffering from? And if it's something of a personal nature, then please let us -- tell us and we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I think it was something with her kidneys, a stone in the kidneys that needed to be examined by ultrasound.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So Milan Lukic told you that he's bringing his mother for an ultrasound examination and he's bringing her to Belgrade to have that done. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he tell you why he was taking her to Belgrade for the ultrasound rather than the hospital that was in Visegrad itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Honestly, I didn't ask, and I am doubtful that we had that sort of thing in Visegrad. It's a small hospital, and if you needed the smallest thing we were referred to Uzice, Foca, Belgrade, any other place. Only the most basic things could be treated in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've mentioned Uzice. There's a full hospital in the town of Uzice. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: It's not really large, but there is a hospital in Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that that's much closer to Visegrad than Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I agree with you, but if you get a referral in Visegrad, Uzice also cannot provide all the treatment that Belgrade can offer. Uzice is mainly for hospitalization, for maternity, delivery, that sort of stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your belief that Uzice might not have had the necessary equipment to conduct an ultrasound examination. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to go back and ask you some questions related to your place of birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So I'd ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, I want to show you a list of names of people from the Zupa area, and just if you could tell me whether you recognize any of the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that 0645-5166 be put up on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you just to look over that list and after you've done, if you could tell me whether or not you recognize any of the names on that list.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
