utterances.text: No, I don't recognize any of the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm finished with that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to return now to your phone conversation with Milan Lukic. At any time during the phone conversation with Milan Lukic or the time that you met him in Novi Pazar, did you ever say to him, How does the farm look, how do the livestock look, are they being cared for? Did you ever ask him how things were on the farm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I didn't ask him at all. I merely inquired about my family. I didn't care about the livestock, and I didn't even assume that it was there. I expected that the livestock had been taken care of. If they had left, I assumed that they had taken the cattle with them, but I didn't ask him that. I assumed that Lukic would not go to my house to check because the houses had been torched, to check, to see whether anything of the sort was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we perhaps redact page 74, lines 20 through to 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd like to put to you some information that I have from the government of Bosnia with respect to MLD2, your brother. The information that I have is that your brother was in Zepa from April 1992 until it fell in July of 1995. Further, that he was a member of the Zepa Brigade of the Army of the Federation of Bosnia, and that your family members lived in a village called Pripecak near Zepa in a vacant house that belonged to a person by the name of Avdo Ramic. Ma'am, I want to ask you again and remind you of your obligation to tell the truth here. Where was your brother in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: In June 1992, my brother was still at Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your position that any other information contrary to that would be mistaken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to speak to you a moment about protective measures. You have requested and you've been granted protective measures, which make it impossible for anyone to know your identity. In the application that was made on your behalf, the following was stated: "In particular, she is afraid of Muslim nationalists, in particular, her" -- and the relative that I think you know who I'm referring to, I won't identify it more precisely than that -- "who is an extreme nationalist and related to some fire victims listed in the present indictment. This relative has a propensity of violence proved by his conviction for killing three individuals following the war." You testified today that this person was convicted of -- or killed two people. Which is it? Is it two or is it three?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that calls for speculation. She's not the author of a submission made by the Defence team at the point where counsel had just gotten into the case and had to meet the deadlines of doing the alibi disclosure -- the protective measures disclosures. It's -- and she said, I believe, in transcript two -- three. So Mr. Groome, if you'd cite the transcript, maybe you'd alleviate the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but she can clarify that. She's not the author of the request for protective measures, but it concerns her. I think she's in a position to provide the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But she's testified three today, so Mr. Groome is misstating her evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologize. I thought she said two.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Page 35, line 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it three that -- three people that he killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Based on the knowledge that I have, the information that I have, I don't know how accurate it was. I heard that two people were killed and three people were wounded and he himself were wounded, too, as the fourth person. They were all BH army members, fighters, soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's two people killed and three people wounded. That's your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. That's the information that I have. Now, I can't vouch for the accuracy of this information because I didn't have the indictment in front of me, the indictment containing the charges against him, but basically that was the incident. That's the knowledge that I have, and I know that he served time in prison for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And then last week, I received a letter from Mr. Alarid saying that Mr. Vilic had killed five and injured 22. So to the knowledge that you have, that's incorrect. Is that not --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would object as to the Prosecutor putting a letter from me or anything in that. That's my supposition, and that was not communicated by this, and I think it's an improper question of the witness. Based on information that I had heard, but we're trying to get the indictment and the judgement and sentence as we speak. We're probably making a Rule 54 application for said judgement and sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why are you putting a letter from counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness has been called to provide this information about Mr. Vilic, and what I am demonstrating is here is that it seems that it goes from two to three to five to 22 injured. I want to explore with this witness, is it she that's exaggerating? True, it is a supposition of Mr. Alarid, and that's my objection to the serious allegations, not only in this particular case not against the Prosecution but against a man who testified here that he killed three more people than he was convicted for. I believe I'm entitled to put to this witness, did she ever tell Mr. Alarid or Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: She didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know. This -- she has not testified to the five. That's not even in evidence. Mr. Groome just brought it in. I don't understand what he's doing with this -- with this -- he's trying to back-door in his own actions as being the basis for his questions. I've never heard of that before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You can put the statement in Mr. Alarid's letter to her [sic] but not what she told Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever state to anyone that Mr. Vilic had killed five people and injured 22 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Never to anyone, and I never made any statements or entered into any polemics or anything. The only thing that I did was I gave a statement to the Defence counsel who came to get a statement from me in defence of Milan Lukic. I never gave any statements anywhere else to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, going back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry. I just see on the transcript where I said, "You can put the statement in Mr. Alarid's letter to her." That should have been Mr. Alarid's letter to you, because that's what you said. So if I said that, I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, again, where you say you were afraid of Muslim nationalists, when Mr. Ivetic asked you to describe what made you fearful, what made you feel intimidated, the first thing you said was that you had many phone calls on your phone, no one ever said anything, but you had many phone calls that you found suspicious. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And once you got a cordless phone, it seemed that the problem was corrected. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And then the other thing that you found suspicious or intimidating or you feared was that you saw vehicles drive down your street that you did not recognize. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever file a report to the police about either of these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I did not because I did not want to. I did not want to reveal myself as a witness. That's why I never reported it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But certainly, couldn't you have just called the police and said -- without revealing that you're a witness and said, I'm receiving phone calls and I see cars that concern me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, you know what? How could I report to the police that I'm seeing unknown cars, unfamiliar cars? The police would tell me, Well, it's a public road, anybody has the right to use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What about seeing cars you did not recognize and having your phone ring, no one answer? What made you think that you had something to fear from Muslim nationalists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, I thought that because all those cars were new cars that I had never noticed passing by before, and I know the people who live around me, people who normally pass by. I recognise them. None of them have very new, shiny cars, so I thought these must be some services.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why not thieves or people engaged in any number of things in the neighborhood? Why Muslim nationalists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Thieves have no reason to do that because they have nothing to steal. It's a rural area where people make their living on farming. They have no capital for thieves to be interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, isn't it correct that despite the protective measures, just the content of your testimony here today, this relative that I've referred to, it'll be clear to that person who are you. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not an objection, but counsel -- if counsel, when that gentleman was here testifying, counsel gave him a pseudonym sheet identifying this witness, so he definitely knows. And when I say counsel, I mean whoever the Prosecutor was that was on direct examination of Mr. Hamdija Vilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'm the one yesterday that was twice -- that was accused of testifying. I think we've heard a bit of testimony from both counsel. If I could just ask the question to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you have any doubt that the person just by the nature of your testimony will realize that it's you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I don't know whether that person hearing what I said would realize it's me, but I suppose he would because I heard that my brother was receiving threats and other things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I don't know, this is the first time in my -- and I'm going on, I think, nine or this is my 10th year, I believe -- 9th year at the Tribunal, this is the first time I've heard witnesses being asked about the protective measures and being attacked about the protective measures that they've sought. That's under the Statute. They're entitled to them --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slow down, please. Slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This honorable Trial Chamber is granted the protective measures that were sought and I think the counsel's question is, at this point, harassment of the witness rather than anything that can be of probative value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't agree at all. It's a perfectly proper question in the circumstances. Answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please answer the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: You know what? If I were unable to receive protective measures -- I sought them for my own safety, and my safety is still in danger if anybody finds out that I appeared here as a witness. If I had not been granted protective measures, then I would have come anyway, come what may.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now ask you about MLD2, who's also scheduled to testify in this case. Did you speak with him prior to coming to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When is the last time you spoke with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Perhaps a year ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And last week was an important Muslim holiday. You didn't call him to exchange greetings or to wish him well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I did not call him lest the information about my testifying should leak, and he doesn't even know that I'm -- that I was to appear as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that your -- MLD2 has no idea, or not at least from you, that you are a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I'm sure he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why are you sure that he doesn't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, he doesn't know from me, for sure. I don't know if he learned from someone else, but certainly not from me. He doesn't know that I'm here or that I will testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness -- let us go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, you must be terribly frightened of Hamdija Vilic if he's the reason why you haven't spoken to your brother in a year. Am I correct in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you've testified earlier that you never told Hamdija Vilic that you were going to be a witness in this case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If you're so fearful of Hamdija Vilic, how is it when he asked you to have a meeting with the Milan Defence team in your home, you actually invite him into your home to have that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Well, I invited him because he said he would come to testify, tell the truth, and give a statement to the lawyers. At that time, I had nothing to fear, not in that connection because he agreed to come, and he was the one who insisted he would only come to my house because he was afraid of balijas, as he called them, in Sarajevo, because he is afraid of Muslims just as I am, and he didn't want to meet with the lawyers in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When's the last time you spoke to Hamdija Vilic before this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: I talked to him when he called me - I don't know where from - and he just said, Are the lawyers still in touch with you, are they calling you, and I said, No, why would they, there's no need, and I hung up. That's how long that conversation lasted, and that was the last time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe that phone call is after the meeting. What I'm talking to you about is prior to the time that he called you up and says, Can I meet with the lawyers in your home. Prior to that phone call, when's the last time you spoke with Hamdija Vilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: That phone call was before his coming here to testify, perhaps a few days before, a couple of days before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'm talking to you about when did he call you up and request for you to invite him to his [sic] home to have a meeting with the Milan Lukic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: One day before, he met with the lawyers for the Defence. He said he would come the next morning. I told him he's free to come the night before and the stay the night in our house. Instead, he came the next day, very early in the morning at 8 or 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did he know that the lawyers were going to be in your house the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Because I told him they were coming, and I asked him whether he preferred for them to come to Sarajevo or for him to come over. It was easier for the lawyers to go to Sarajevo, but he insisted that he wouldn't meet them in Sarajevo, that he would meet them instead at my place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If he doesn't know that you're a witness in the case, why does he call you to make contact with the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Because I asked him if he was willing to -- in fact, the lawyers asked me if Hamdija Vilic was going to testify. I conveyed that to him, and he said, yes, he would, and that's why he got in touch with me to contact them, because the lawyers did not have his number. They were not able to contact him themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When did you ask Hamdija Vilic if he was willing to testify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Just the day before the lawyers came, the day before he arrived and the lawyers came to my house as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you called him and asked him whether he's willing to testify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes, and he said he was willing, that he was going to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So, again -- let's see if I understand this. This person who you are so fearful of that you have broken off contact with your brother, you call him to ask him if he's willing to be a witness in the Milan Lukic case, for the Defence, and you invite him to stay in your home, to sleep there the night before the meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes. But at that time, I had no reason to fear his visit. I just asked him nicely if he wanted to be a witness. He said yes. He just said that he wanted protection measures, that he wanted to testify but not in public, and there was no problem. I had no reason to be afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But, ma'am, you've told us that you broke off contact -- or you haven't had contact with your brother in a year, and it's because of his relationship with Hamdija Vilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, one of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because Hamdija Vilic lives close --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Let's hear counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to speak for Mr. Groome but one of my fears is that this line of questioning began right at the point where he asked him [sic], Did you call your brother for a Muslim holiday, a recent one, and then that backed up into the year, I guess. And I want to know if there's some confusion and if counsel could clarify for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And it misstates her testimony as saying she was only afraid of Hamdija Vilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm now confused. Proceed, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, there seems to be some confusion over what you're giving evidence about now, so let me see if I can clarify it. As you sit here, taking today's date, is it true that have you not spoken to your brother, MLD2, for one year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Correct. Correct. I stand behind -- by what I said. I have not talked to my brother in that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, when Judge Robinson asked you why that was, did you not say that that was because of your brother's relationship with Hamdija Vilic, who you are fearful of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Correct. Hamdija Vilic lives close to my brother. He calls on him often. They are friends, and that's why I do not dare contact my brother. My brother might say that I talked to him, and he might reveal that I was going to be a witness. That's why I did not contact him. There's no other reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when you had the meeting with the Defence team, the date that I've been told that occurred was sometime in June, when you had that meeting, the night before -- or I'm sorry. You invited Hamdija Vilic to stay in your home, to sleep in your home, in advance of that meeting, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: Yes, unless he's able to come early in the morning, I told him, You can come and stay the night. I invited him as a relative because he had said already he was going to be a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, I put it to you that the reason that you no longer speak to your brother is that you were paid 21.000 Euros to secure his testimony, that you only gave him 5.000 Euros of the money that you received and you kept the rest, and that when he found out about that he became very angry with you and he has refused to speak with you. Isn't that really what's happened here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: That's not true. I never received, not only 21.000 Euros, I never received a single mark. As for Hamdija Vilic and his ilk are making up, has he seen me get any money? I don't understand what kind of story that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, it's not only Hamdija Vilic. There is another person who makes a very similar claim. Are you denying that you've received any money -- let's just confine ourselves to MLD2. Are you denying that you received any money to secure the testimony of MLD2?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no foundation for the question unless he specifies who the other person is and the basis for the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The question is: "Are you denying that you received any money to secure the testimony of MLD2?"

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why does that need a foundation?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, because it's tied together with his previous statement that says, "Ma'am, it's not only Hamdija Vilic. There's another person who makes a very similar claim." If counsel is going to make a representation like that, I'd like to get a citation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but the question itself isn't necessarily relate to that. The witness can answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand. Which question am I supposed to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If it assists the Court, I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Reformulate, and then we'll have to stop after this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'm putting it to you as plainly as I can that you have received money in order to buy the testimony of your brother, MLD2, and that the reason that he no longer speaks with you is because he discovered that you kept some of the money that you were given to buy his testimony. He feels cheated by you and no longer wants to come and testify. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD10
utterances.text: That's not true. My brother was a witness and said would be a witness even before I knew it. Even before I was aware of such a possibility, he told me that he was going to come to testify. He was the one who volunteered the information. I heard from him that he was going to be a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, we're going to adjourn. I have some matters to deal with. Witness, that concludes your testimony for today. For today. You will have to return when we resume in January, and that will be Wednesday, January 14th, at 2.15 p.m. Wednesday, January the 14th. Now, I have to tell you that during the break, this will be a break of about three and a half weeks, you are not to discuss your evidence with anybody. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may leave now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, my concern is this, is we have the witness here, and I'm not sure what Mr. Groome had in terms of additional cross-examination, but it seems wasteful if it wasn't going to be significant that we don't complete it before the witness leaves town, considering the long break. It's not just a weekend. It's three and a half weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, how much more did you have in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have a fair bit, and if you'll recall from earlier on, with some of the surprises that occurred during the testimony, I would like the benefit of the additional time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. So the position will remain the same. I have a decision to give. On the 12th of December, 2008, the Prosecution filed a motion seeking an order to bar the alibi-related evidence of several witnesses for Milan Lukic in total or in part. The Prosecution argues that the Defence of Milan Lukic has not met its obligations to notify the Prosecution of the alibi witnesses pursuant to Rule 67. The motion is premature in view of the fact that the final witness list of Milan Lukic is to be filed by the 5th of January, 2009. It is therefore dismissed without prejudice to the Prosecution making further witness-specific objections if necessary once the witness list has been filed. The Trial Chamber is seized of the Prosecution's request -- I should have said that that's the end of that decision. The second matter is this. The Trial Chamber is seized of the Prosecution's request for clarification of confidential classification of contempt proceedings and motion to leave to exceed word limit in response to oral submissions of 9th December, 2008, and related submissions of 12th December, 2008. This was filed on the 16th of December. The Chamber orders the Defence to file its response to the remaining matter contained in this motion, namely the clarification of confidential classification of contempt proceedings by 4 p.m. tomorrow. Now, I want to say additionally that we have had some exchanges between counsel which have been -- I describe them as relatively heated. I don't want to have a repetition. I am fully accustomed to vigorous Prosecution and vigorous Defence, but I expect counsel to behave with equanimity. Counsel should always remember that counsel is an officer of the court, whose primary duty is the pursuit of justice and to assist the Chamber in its work. So I do not wish to have a repeat of the heated exchanges which have taken place between counsel. Is there any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's a matter that I raised yesterday, and it's the difficulty of preparing for our work when we still don't have the witness list. Under the rules, it should have been provided prior to the commencement of trial. Now we're going to -- it seems like we're going to receive it well beyond that and just prior to restarting. Again, I bear the burden of disproving this alibi, and it's very difficult to do that without the witness list as required by the rules. I'm therefore requesting, I know there are a number of things that the Chamber's order had required of the Defence by the 5th of January, including better summaries. I would ask to request that the Chamber prior to the break, prior to tomorrow afternoon, that Defence be required at least to tell us who the 45 witnesses that they are going to call so that we can begin our preparations. Right now, it stands at 90. As I said yesterday, it's a tremendous waste of resources. It's difficult to do with people taking their holidays over the break for me to have people working on this. It puts us at a disadvantage. It's against the rules, and I would ask you to at least require them to let us know who the witnesses are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Respectfully, Your Honour, we would simply ask that the January 5th order that's in place or the order for January 5th final witness list be kept in place. Mr. Ivetic is going to be working over the holidays in the region trying to do exactly what the Court requests, and we anticipate being able to comply with the Court with that time. Doing it by tomorrow would make it really difficult for us to comply with the Court's request today that we file before 4 p.m. tomorrow as well as Judge Bonomy who's required submissions by tomorrow as well. So, under the -- the totality of the circumstances, I don't think the state's particularly prejudiced considering the trial began in this case on July 9th, and they didn't file their final witness list until July 17th, and there were several motions to amend that list over the course of time that we dealt with appropriately. So in a grand-scheme-of-things approach, it would be disingenuous for us to say we can get that done by tomorrow without probably stepping on our own toes a little bit later, considering it's premature for us as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we're trying to find a fair solution, Mr. Alarid and Mr. Groome, and we think it is this, that the Defence be required to file the first ten witnesses by the 26th of December and the remaining 35 by the 5th of January, by the 5th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We can do that, Your Honour. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. We are adjourned, and have a merry Christmas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 14th day of January, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25
